Every path the diff reaches is outside the implicit touch points (docs/specs/**, INDEX.md, docs/process/reviews/**): .githooks/pre-push, .process-kit.lock, docs/process/codex.md and CLAUDE.md. Each is reported as an unplanned touch point.

The new pre-push early exit is a deliberate skip of precheck, classification and traceability for deletion-only pushes. The hook's own comments and printed message describe it accurately, so no comment-versus-code defect is reported.
potential_unspecified_behavior: A push that only deletes refs now exits 0 before precheck, classification and traceability, including a deletion of protected branches develop or main. Nothing in the repository specifies whether that skip is intended. docs/process/prohibited.md treats a gate bypass as prohibited. Whether this counts as loosening a check is a design judgement for a human.

In a mixed push, a deletion of a protected branch no longer sets PROTECTED_PUSH, because the deletion line hits `continue` at pre-push:30 before line 33. Only the update lines decide whether traceability runs.

A ref deletion sent to a protected branch now produces only the message 'deletion only, checks skipped' and no traceability record, and nothing specifies what the traceability check should say about a deleted protected branch.
regression_risks: Any future change to the REFS/UPDATES loop at .githooks/pre-push:26-39 can silently make ordinary pushes skip all checks, and no test in this repository would catch it.
Removing the early exit later, or adding a branch to it, would change which pushes run traceability, and no test pins the current behavior.

The lock hash for .githooks/pre-push (108ffb6d...) and for docs/process/codex.md (0a544a27...) would no longer match if either file is edited, which the next kit update or classification would not catch.
test_coverage: No test in this repository runs .githooks/pre-push. Grep of scripts/**, tests/** and .github/** finds only the hooksPath warning in scripts/process/review.sh:573-574. The kit says it is tested in its own repository, which this review cannot see.
The new deletion-only branch (pre-push:36-39) and the mixed-push case (pre-push:30) have no test here, so either could be inverted without a failing check.
